question.problem: A fair six-sided die is rolled $12$ times. What is the variance of the number of times we get a number less than $3?$
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of time we get a number less than $3.$

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=12$ rolls

- the probability of getting a number less than $3$ (i.e., a $1$ or $2$) on any roll of the die is

$$
p=\frac{2}{6}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(12,\frac{1}{3}).$

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the variance is given by

$$
\text{Var}[X]=np(1-p),
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the variance of the number of times we get a number less than $3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =np(1-p) \\  & =12\cdot \frac{1}{3}\cdot (1-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =4\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
